purpose: Budtender training guide (budtender-guide.html on the-reefer.com). Owner direction, November 28, 2026: what front-line budtenders need to know so a customer never has to name a product category to get help. The spine is a six-step intake in the owner's order: what they want out of it, their requirements, beliefs to clear up, their preference, the pros and cons of each form when they have none, and the strains customers commonly report for that use. Facts carry a named source with the date it was checked; strain notes are breeder descriptions or user reports, labeled as such, never medical claims.
promise: Never make a customer name a category. Ask about the experience they want, and you name the category.

intake.title: What do you want out of it?
ask: What are you hoping it does for you?
Is this for a time of day, like evenings or weekends?
Anything you're trying to get help with?
intake.listen: Listen for the outcome, not a product word: sleep, stress, aches, fun with friends, focus, appetite, or as little high as possible.
intake.why: The goal decides strength and timing before you ever say flower or gummy. If someone mentions a health condition, take it as their goal in their words. You aren't diagnosing, and you can't promise relief.

intake.title: What are your requirements?
ask: Is smoke okay, or do you need smoke-free?
Does it need to be discreet?
How fast do you want to feel it, and how long should it last?
intake.listen: Each answer rules forms in or out. Smoke-free rules out flower and pre-rolls. Fast rules out edibles. All night favors something swallowed.
intake.why: Requirements are hard limits. Settle them first so you only show things that can work.

intake.title: What have you heard?
ask: Have you tried anything before? How did it go?
Anything you've heard that you want to avoid, or want to try?
intake.listen: Listen for the common beliefs below. Clear them up gently, without making anyone feel dumb.
intake.why: A bad first experience usually starts with a belief, like taking a second gummy because the first one didn't hit yet.

intake.title: Do you already have a favorite way?
ask: Do you already know how you like to take it?
Any flavor, brand or strain you liked before?
intake.listen: If they have a preference, go straight to it and narrow by strength, size, flavor and price.
intake.why: Respect what they know. Don't send a happy flower customer through the whole speech.

intake.title: No preference? Walk through the options
ask: Want me to walk you through the main options? It takes a minute.
intake.listen: Use the product cards below: how it works, how fast, how long, pros and cons. Offer two or three that fit their requirements, not all eight.
intake.why: This is the part customers are really asking for when they say they don't know what they want.

intake.title: Point them to what others report
ask: Here's what people often pick for that. The lab report for this batch tells us more than the name does.
intake.listen: Offer names customers commonly ask for, then check the batch label for THC, CBD and terpenes.
intake.why: A strain name and an indica or sativa label are weak predictors. Frame names as what other customers report, never as a promise.

goals.label: Wind down or sleep
goals.steer: Later in the day, longer lasting. Swallowed forms last longest; a low dose to start.

goals.label: Take the edge off stress
goals.steer: Start low. Too much THC can bring on anxiety, so a lower THC or balanced THC:CBD product is a fair first step.

goals.label: Body aches or soreness
goals.steer: Ask what they've tried. Topicals, tinctures and edibles are common asks. Their doctor is the one to weigh in on pain treatment.

goals.label: Social, fun, upbeat
goals.steer: Quick and short: a pre-roll to share, a low-dose gummy or a drink, at a pace they can manage.

goals.label: Daytime, focus or creative
goals.steer: Low dose and short acting, so they stay functional. Inhaled forms wear off soonest.

goals.label: Appetite
goals.steer: Ask about timing: before a meal points to something fast acting.

goals.label: As little high as possible
goals.steer: CBD-dominant or balanced products, low THC per serving. Remind them CBD products can still contain some THC.

requirements.steer: Edibles, drinks, tinctures, capsules or topicals. Vapes are smoke-free but still inhaled.
Gummies, capsules, tinctures and drinks look like everyday items and give off no smoke. Remind them to store them away from children.
Inhaled forms start in seconds to minutes. Edibles can take up to 2 hours.
Swallowed forms last about 4 to 8 hours; inhaled forms about 2 to 4.
Ask for a number. Then compare by milligrams of THC per dollar or by the gram, not by the sticker price.
Be honest: any THC product can lead to a positive test, CBD products included. The US Department of Transportation says CBD use is no excuse for a positive.

notions.myth: Indica means couch, sativa means energy.
notions.fact: A study of nearly 90,000 flower samples from six states found the labels don't consistently match the chemistry; samples labeled indica, sativa and hybrid were highly intermingled.
notions.say: Those labels are a rough start. The lab report on this batch tells us more.

notions.fact: Health Canada advises new users to start under 10% THC for inhaled products and to take the most care above 20%, which includes shatter, wax and distillates.
notions.say: More THC means more chance of a rough time. Let's match the strength to your experience.

notions.myth: The edible didn't hit, so take another.
notions.fact: Swallowed cannabis can take 30 minutes to 2 hours to start working and peaks after 2 to 4 hours. That delay is why people take too much.
notions.say: Give it at least two hours before you take more.

notions.myth: It's the same stuff I smoked years ago.
notions.fact: In federal testing of seized cannabis, average THC rose from about 4% in 1995 to about 16% in 2022.
notions.say: Today's flower is a lot stronger than what you remember. Start lower than you think.

notions.myth: CBD can't show up on a drug test.
notions.fact: The US Department of Transportation warns that CBD labels can be misleading, products may contain more THC than stated, and CBD use is no excuse for a confirmed positive.
notions.say: If you're tested, there's no product I can promise won't show.

notions.myth: A cart is a cart, wherever you get it.
notions.fact: In the 2019 vaping lung injury outbreak, 82% of patients reported using THC vapes, vitamin E acetate was strongly linked, and the CDC warned against THC vapes from informal sources such as friends or dealers.
notions.say: Licensed carts are tested and tracked. Street carts aren't.

notions.myth: The strain name guarantees the effect.
notions.fact: Evidence that terpenes and other compounds steer the effect in people, the so-called entourage effect, is still early, with simple and contradictory studies.
notions.say: People report patterns, but every body is different. Let's start small and you tell me how it goes.

forms.name: Flower
forms.how: Dried buds, smoked in a pipe, bong or joint or heated in a dry herb vaporizer.
pros: Fast, so it's easy to stop when you've had enough
Widest choice of strains and prices
You can smell and see what you're buying
cons: Smoke and smell
Needs gear: papers, a pipe or a vaporizer
Dose is less exact
forms.fit: People who want control and speed, and don't mind smoke.

forms.name: Pre-rolls
forms.how: Flower already rolled into a joint. Infused pre-rolls add concentrate and are much stronger.
pros: Ready to go, no gear but a lighter
Small sizes are a cheap way to try a strain
cons: Smoke and smell
You can't see the flower inside
Infused ones surprise new users
forms.fit: Social use, trying a strain, people who don't roll.

forms.name: Vapes and carts
forms.how: A cartridge of cannabis oil on a battery, or an all-in-one disposable. Heated, not burned.
pros: One puff at a time makes pacing easy
cons: Usually far stronger than flower
Needs a compatible battery
Buy licensed only: the 2019 lung injury outbreak was tied to THC vapes, many from informal sources
forms.fit: Discreet, quick use by people who are comfortable with stronger products.

forms.name: Concentrates
forms.how: Resin pulled from the plant into wax, shatter, badder, rosin or live resin, dabbed with a rig or a concentrate vaporizer.
pros: A little goes a long way
Strong flavor in live resin and rosin
Good value per milligram for experienced users
cons: Very strong: Health Canada puts products over 20% THC in its most-caution band
Needs special gear
Not a first-timer product

forms.name: Edibles and gummies
forms.how: Food with cannabis in it, digested before it works. The liver changes THC into a form called 11-hydroxy-THC.
cons: Slow start, so people take too much
Hard to stop once it's working
Look like candy: store away from kids
forms.fit: Smoke-free, discreet, long-lasting use. Start at 2.5 mg THC if new.

forms.name: Drinks
forms.how: Cannabis in a beverage. It's swallowed, so it behaves like an edible.
cons: Still slow to start
Don't mix with alcohol: it adds to impairment
forms.fit: People who want a social, low-dose option.

forms.name: Tinctures, oils and capsules
forms.how: Liquid drops or capsules. Held under the tongue, drops start sooner; swallowed, they act like an edible.
forms.onset: 15 to 40 minutes under the tongue; 30 minutes to 2 hours swallowed
forms.lasts: Up to about 12 hours under the tongue
pros: Easy to adjust a drop at a time
cons: Taste of some oils
Still slower than inhaling
Read the label: drops per serving vary
forms.fit: Careful dosing, CBD-curious and medical customers.

forms.name: Topicals
forms.how: Creams, balms and lotions applied to the skin.
pros: Applied right where they want it
cons: Health Canada says there isn't yet enough information on timing, duration or risks
Don't promise a body effect like an edible
forms.fit: People who want something on the skin, not a high.

examples.name: Northern Lights
examples.note: Weedmaps reviewers describe physical relaxation, with sleepiness a frequent report.

strains.tip: Whatever the strain, a later time of day and a swallowed form matter more for an all-night effect.

examples.name: Durban Poison
examples.note: Weedmaps reviewers describe a fast, bright high with energy, focus and creativity.

examples.name: Jack Herer
examples.note: Weedmaps reviewers most often report uplifted, happy and relaxed. Sensi Seeds, its breeder, says one version of the plant is the most energetic and another the most physical.

strains.tip: Keep the dose low for daytime so they stay functional.

examples.name: Blue Dream
examples.note: Humboldt Seed Organization, a breeder of one Blue Dream line, describes a clear, long-lasting cerebral effect.

strains.tip: Shared pre-rolls and low-dose drinks are easy ways to pace a group.

examples.name: ACDC
examples.note: About 20 parts CBD to 1 part THC; Weedmaps reviewers most often report relaxed, happy and uplifted.

examples.name: Harlequin
examples.note: Project CBD lists it among early CBD-rich strains at about 3 parts CBD to 2 parts THC.

examples.name: Cannatonic
examples.note: Its breeder, Resin Seeds, says plants range from 30:1 THC:CBD to 1:30, so the batch label decides.

strains.tip: CBD-rich flower is rare: 96.5% of the tested flower in that six-state study was THC-dominant. Balanced tinctures and gummies are easier to find.

start_low.title: Edibles
start_low.text: New users: 2.5 mg THC or less. 2.5 to 10 mg, use caution. 10 mg or more, the most caution.

start_low.title: Inhaled
start_low.text: Start with 1 or 2 puffs and wait before taking more.

start_low.title: Inhaled strength
start_low.text: New users: under 10% THC, with equal or more CBD. 10% to 20%, use caution. Over 20%, the most caution.

start_low.title: Drops
start_low.text: Start with 1 drop and go up one drop at a time.

scenarios.says: "I've never done this. What should I get?"
scenarios.ask: What do you want it to do? Smoke okay? Do you want to feel it fast or slow?
scenarios.steer: A low-dose gummy (2.5 mg) or one or two puffs of low-THC flower. Explain the edible wait out loud.

scenarios.says: "I used to smoke in college. Give me the strongest."
scenarios.ask: When did you last use it? What did you like then?
scenarios.steer: Tell them average THC roughly quadrupled since the mid-1990s. Steer to moderate flower and go up from there.

scenarios.says: "My doctor said this could help with my back."
scenarios.ask: What has your doctor suggested? What have you tried? Do you take other medicines?
scenarios.steer: Match their requirements and comfort level. Send medicine-interaction questions to their doctor or pharmacist; CBD and THC can both interact.

scenarios.says: "It's for my dad. He's never tried it."
scenarios.ask: What does he want it to do? Does he smoke? Any health issues or medicines he's mentioned?
scenarios.steer: Smoke-free and low dose, with the timing written down. Remind them that only adults 21 and over may buy, and to store it away from kids.

scenarios.says: "Last time I got way too high and freaked out."
scenarios.ask: What did you take, how much, and how fast did it hit?
scenarios.steer: Usually too much THC or a second edible too soon. Offer lower THC, a balanced THC:CBD product, and the start-low rules.

scenarios.ask: What's your number, and how do you like to use it?
scenarios.steer: Compare by THC milligrams per dollar or price per gram. Larger flower sizes, value brands and daily deals.

scenarios.says: "I can't have it smell. I live with my parents."
scenarios.ask: Smoke-free okay? How long do you need it to last?
scenarios.steer: Gummies, capsules or tinctures. No smoke, no smell, exact doses.

scenarios.says: "Will CBD show up on a test?"
scenarios.ask: Do you get tested for work?
scenarios.steer: Be straight: CBD products can contain THC and can cause a positive. Don't promise any product is test-safe.

bad: Hi, I'm looking for something to help me relax after work.
Okay. Flower, carts, edibles or concentrates?
I don't really know. Whatever's good?
Well, you have to tell me what you want.
good: Hi, I'm looking for something to help me relax after work.
Got it, wind down after work. Is smoke okay, or would you rather not?
I'd rather not. And I've only tried it a couple of times.
Then I'd look at a low-dose gummy or a tincture. Gummies take 30 minutes to 2 hours to kick in and last a few hours, so take one around dinner and wait. Want a 2.5 milligram to start?

rules.title: Check ID on every sale
rules.text: Ohio requires a dispensary employee to review a valid government photo ID with a date of birth before any adult-use sale, and confirm the buyer is 21 or older.

rules.title: Know the daily limit
rules.text: Ohio's adult-use daily limit is 2.5 ounces of plant material and no more than 15,000 mg of total THC. Other states differ.

rules.title: Don't drive high
rules.text: Say it plainly with every edible, and don't mix with alcohol, which adds to impairment.

rules.title: Lock it up at home
rules.text: Edibles can be mistaken for normal food. Tell customers with kids or pets to store products locked away.

rules.title: Know who to call
rules.text: If someone has worrying symptoms after taking cannabis, US Poison Control is 1-800-222-1222. For an emergency, call 911.

rules.title: Leave medical calls to clinicians
rules.text: Don't diagnose or promise relief. CBD can have side effects and interact with medicines, so send those questions to a doctor or pharmacist.

rules.title: Use your store's materials
rules.text: Ohio dispensaries must keep educational materials on substance abuse and access to addiction services. Know where yours are.
